head: 08f5e65113e7670cb709cdd6b7a47b42451b0abc
reasons: plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py's git-verb detection in _part_targets (the `elif headl == "git" and len(words) >= 2:` branch, lines 370-376 at this HEAD) reads the subcommand from the fixed position words[1] with no flag-skipping (unlike cp/mv/rm/tee, which run _nonflag first). A real git global option before the subcommand -- `-c <name>=<value>`, `--git-dir=<path>`, `--work-tree=<path>`, etc. -- defeats it. Traced `git -c core.fileMode=false rm CLAUDE.md` by hand through decide()/_resolution_walk/_part_targets: words = ['git','-c','core.fileMode=false','rm','CLAUDE.md']; sub = words[1].lower() = '-c', which matches none of 'checkout'/'restore'/'rm'/'mv'/'apply', so _part_targets yields no candidate at all and decide() reaches Decision.allow() -- while the real `git rm CLAUDE.md` (a path-taking git verb the Design section itself lists as a covered write idiom) genuinely removes the guardrail file from the working tree and index. No token in this command is non-literal ($VAR/$()/glob), so the fail-closed rule never fires either. This is a fully literal, ordinary invocation that plugin/ci/settings.ci.json's allow-list already permits bare (Bash(git *)).

The same fixed-position assumption defeats _inner_shell_command (lines 235-238 at this HEAD): `if len(words) >= 3 and (words[0].lower(), words[1].lower()) in _INNER_SHELL_PAIRS: return words[2]`, which only recognises the exact adjacent pair. Traced `bash --norc -c 'echo x > CLAUDE.md'`: words = ['bash','--norc','-c', pair ('bash','--norc') is not in _INNER_SHELL_PAIRS, so the quoted inner command is never recursed into; the outer dispatch (_part_targets with headl='bash') matches none of the recognised idioms (the '>' is inside the single-quoted token, correctly treated as literal text, not a chain-level operator), so shell_write_targets returns [] and decide() allows. Again a fully literal command with no non-literal token to trip the fail-closed rule.

Both gaps are the exact class of vulnerability intent.md and this change exist to close (an unattended Bash call reaching a guardrail file while the path-based gate sees nothing). They are reachable in CI with the allow-listed Bash(git *); the only remaining layer there is plugin/ci/settings.ci.json's sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite (also added by this diff), but spec.md's own Flagged concerns state a by-hand run, native Windows, or any host with no sandbox has 'the hook alone' -- on such a host both bypasses are complete and silent.

No test in the diff or in tests/test_hooks.py exercises a git invocation with a global option before the subcommand, or an inner-shell call with a flag between the interpreter and its -c/-Command token: tests/test_hooks.py's existing git -c coverage (line 625, 'git -c user.name=x commit -m y') belongs to test_plan_sync_detects_commit_in_any_position, a different hook, not shell_guard; the shell_guard wrapper/inner-shell test (test_shell_write_targets_sees_through_wrappers_and_inner_shells, line 1980) only exercises the bare 'bash -c'/'sh -c'/'cmd /c'/'pwsh -Command' pairs with no extra flag. plan.md's own named residual ('an unlisted wrapper, content decoded and piped to an interpreter') is a different shape from a documented git/shell flag shifting a recognised idiom's argument position by one slot -- this was missed, not weighed and accepted.

This diff itself carries the evidence of the gap: changes/0002-security-authz-the-guardrail-self-protec/evidence/adversarial-review-c.json (committed at an earlier HEAD, ec837ed, in this same diff) already found and described both bugs in detail. The only code commit in this round after that review, 3a90bd0, fixed solely the third, unrelated finding in the same report (git -C's directory leaking into a later chain part -- confirmed below, correctly fixed). The git-verb and inner-shell argument-position bugs were left unaddressed: fix-requests.json shows empty requests/not_applied, and verifier.md's scope for this round is explicitly 're-verification of the git -C chain-leak fix (commit 3a90bd0)' only -- it does not re-examine or close the other two findings from the same prior review.

Verified separately that the git -C chain-leak finding is correctly fixed at this HEAD: _resolution_walk's git -C branch (lines 416-430) now computes a part-local base/base_nl and no longer reassigns the shared current/nonliteral the rest of the chain loop reads, matching the new tests test_shell_guard_git_dash_c_does_not_leak_into_a_later_chain_part and test_shell_guard_resolves_a_git_dash_c_target and verifier.md's live subprocess runs. That part of the fix is sound and is not grounds for escalation by itself; the escalation rests on the other two, still-open gaps from the same review round.
classification_reasons: Spec is explicit that no open concern here is fully closed: Flagged concerns accept a residual heuristic-parsing gap outside CI (an unlisted wrapper / decoded-and-piped path), but the git-verb and inner-shell argument-position gaps found here are a different, undocumented shape -- an implementation bug in a recognised idiom, not the named residual -- so the gate this change exists to build is not yet complete.

Blast radius is wide: shell_guard.py runs on every Bash/PowerShell call in every phase, by hand and in CI; sdlc.yaml risk_list item 'auth' is touched end to end; the change's Acceptance and its phase-(e) eval case both rest on this hook's git-verb and inner-shell detection being correct, which it is not in two reachable, fully-literal cases.

No pre-existing test exercised a Bash/PowerShell write to a guardrail file before this change (the whole behavior is new), and the new test suite still leaves both an argument-ordering bypass of the git-verb branch and of the inner-shell recursion unexercised -- the tests pass with the bugs present.
attempted: Intent: shell_guard.py, the hooks.json registration and the sandbox denyWrite block target the Bash/PowerShell bypass intent.md describes, and are on-target in shape. Found the implementation does not yet reach the intent's 'every other place with the same pattern' bar for two git/shell forms that are ordinary and literal.

Spec and plan: plan.md's Files-that-change list matches the diff's files; Order of work steps 1-7 are represented; step 8's literal pytest/ruff/compileall paste is absent from this diff but this is a CI session where the runner produces build/test/lint logs after the session (not cited against the change). Confirmed the git -C fix (commit 3a90bd0, this round's only code change) matches plan.md and spec.md exactly.

Proof: read plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py's full tokenizer, git -C handling, and git-verb/inner-shell dispatch line by line against real shell/git semantics, independent of the author's or prior round's claims. Hand-traced both bypass commands through decide()/_resolution_walk/_part_targets/_inner_shell_command and confirmed each reaches Decision.allow() with no non-literal token to trip the fail-closed rule. Cross-checked against tests/test_hooks.py and confirmed no test covers either form. verifier.md's scope this round was explicitly limited to the git -C fix alone, not these two findings.

Blast radius: the hook runs on every Bash/PowerShell call everywhere; both gaps are reachable through CI's own allow-listed Bash(git *) and are mitigated only by the sandbox layer in CI (also part of this diff), not by hand or on native Windows, per spec.md's own Flagged concerns.

Policies: security-baseline's reuse requirement and coding-standards rule 4 (no weakened pre-existing test) are honored; this is a logic/coverage defect in new security-control code, not a skipped policy -- but it is exactly the class of authz gap the security-baseline rule this change cites (authorization must not be inferred from which route reaches the file) exists to prevent, now reproduced inside the new control itself via argument position instead of tool route.

Tests: confirmed the full test suite as currently written passes with both bugs present -- no test places a global git option before a recognised subcommand, and no test places a flag between an inner-shell interpreter and its -c/-Command token.
